problem: Training-free graph-based navigation methods such as UniGoal cannot detect complex loop patterns beyond simple geometric proximity, so they explore redundantly. They also lack temporal coherence in the scene representation, which makes goal recognition inconsistent across viewpoints in instance-image navigation.
motivation: Instance-image navigation requires telling apart visually similar instances of the same category, and the same instance looks very different across viewpoints and lighting. Foundation-model-based zero-shot navigators re-visit areas and sometimes pass the target without recognizing it, which hurts both success and path efficiency.
key_idea: Add a temporal graph memory (TeRM) that links scene-graph nodes across time, and a persistent-homology-based loop detector (TSLC) on agent trajectories, to the UniGoal zero-shot pipeline.
insight: Both modules are training-free add-ons to the UniGoal baseline, and each helps a different aspect. In the 200-episode HM3D ablation, removing TSLC costs more SPL (28.38 to 25.48) than removing TeRM (28.38 to 28.28), while removing TeRM costs more in SR than removing TSLC's SR contribution suggests is needed. This suggests loop avoidance mainly improves path efficiency, while temporal memory mainly improves goal recognition. The ablation is small (200 episodes), so the gains are indicative rather than conclusive.
method: TeRM sliding-window memory: keeps the last K=100 scene-graph snapshots with discount factor gamma=0.95 and builds temporal edges between consecutive snapshots.
Cross-temporal instance linking: a temporal edge between nodes is added if sim>tau, with weight gamma*exp(-lambda*||f_i-f_j||) based on visual-feature change.
Instance similarity: sim = alpha*1[label match] + (1-alpha)*exp(-||p_i-p_j||/sigma_p), fusing semantic label agreement and 3D position closeness.
Velocity estimation and prediction: per-instance velocity from consecutive positions, linear extrapolation of future positions, and temporal context retrieval by semantic label.

TSLC trajectory embedding: poses (x,y,theta) are mapped to [x,y,0.5 sin(theta)], a Vietoris-Rips complex is built with eps_max=5 m up to dimension 2, and PD1 is computed with GUDHI, keeping features with persistence >0.1.

TSLC signature matching: current and historical trajectory segments are compared with the 2-Wasserstein distance (Hungarian matching) combined with persistence-landscape L2 (0.7*W2+0.3*landscape). A loop is flagged when distance < theta_W=2.0, computed every 10 steps, and flagged locations are blacklisted; features can optionally be augmented with SVD-3 projected visual features.
Base pipeline (from UniGoal): GroundingDINO detection, LLaMA as LLM, LLaVA as VLM, CLIP text encoder for graph matching, occupancy map with a deterministic local policy.

setting.backbone: UniGoal pipeline: GroundingDINO + LLaMA (LLM) + LLaVA (VLM) + CLIP text encoder (all frozen)
setting.observation: egocentric RGB-D with GPS and pose (coordinate and orientation), plus a goal image
setting.action_space: low-level discrete: forward, turn-left, turn-right, stop
setting.privileged: none (GPS/pose inputs as in the standard IIN setup)

numbers.extra: training-free; RGBD++ input (coordinate and orientation); success radius 1.0 m

numbers_note: The split name is not stated explicitly; 'val' is assumed for HM3D IIN. The ablation table's naming 'w/o TeRM' (SR 74.99 / SPL 28.28) and 'w/o TSLC' (72.22 / 25.48) is inconsistent with the text, which reports +8.8/+3.5 for TeRM and +6.1/+0.7 for TSLC.
results: On HM3D instance-image navigation, T2-Nav reaches SR 72.6 and SPL 27.8, beating the training-free UniGoal (60.2/23.7) by +12.4/+4.1. It also beats the best supervised method IEVE (70.2/25.2) without any task-specific training.
limitations: VLM/LLM inference overhead makes the full pipeline unsuitable for real-time on-robot operation; the authors state this is shared with the baseline.
Evaluated only in simulation on HM3D indoor scenes; outdoor terrain and multi-floor buildings are untested, and there are no real-robot experiments.
The ablation uses only 200 episodes, and its table is inconsistent with the text; many hyperparameters (alpha, lambda, tau, sigma_p, theta_W) are empirically tuned.
